title: Asynchronous code review cheatsheet + post-merge actions
content:
Context / goal:
Quick personal reference for asynchronous reviews (what to check quickly vs what needs a synchronous session), plus a short list of follow-ups to attach to PRs before merge. Meant for small-to-medium diffs in the serving runtime and batch/caching codepaths.

Quick heuristics (first pass, ~5–15m):
- Read PR description + summary: does it explain user-visible change, perf impact, and rollback? If not, request clarification.
- Diff size check: <200 LOC: do a focused review; 200–800 LOC: sample key files, ask for guided walkthrough; >800 LOC: request split or a synchronous walkthrough.
- Tests present? Unit + integration required for behavior changes. If none, ask for at least a smoke test or test plan.
- CI status: green required. If flaky test history, request re-run and add flaky-test tag.
- Security/sensitive data: search for logging/printfs that might print token/KV contents. Flag immediately.

Async checklist (what I actually scan):
1) Public API / surface: ensure no breaking changes; verify version pin or adapter added if behaviour changes.
2) Core algorithm changes: look for comments explaining why (perf tradeoffs, numerical stability, memory).
3) Error handling: are error paths covered? Are we converting internal errors to proper user-facing codes?
4) Resource management: GPU memory alloc/free, tensor lifecycle, cache invalidation, file handles.
5) Telemetry hooks: do we emit metrics for latency, qps, cache hit-rate, and error counts? Add TODO if missing.
6) Config defaults: sensible defaults that don’t enable risky behavior in prod (autoscale, batching size).
7) Backwards compatibility: model checkpoints, KV cache formats, model metadata.
8) Performance regressions: look for sync points, extra copies, new allocations in hot paths.

Edge cases & targeted tests to request (specific to serving/runtime):
- Large-sequence/few-sequence extremes: test 16 vs 2048 token flows to catch O(seq^2) regressions.
- KV cache reuse across continuations: assert identical logits after cache warmup vs cold start.
- Mixed-precision/quantized model paths: run through fp32 vs int8 to ensure numeric stability.
- Batching interleaving: ensure per-request context isn’t leaking across batch boundaries (use randomized concurrency stress test).
- Prefix-caching invalidation: add test where cached prefix updated on new request and ensure subsequent requests use correct prefix.
- OOM simulator: add a dev-only test that simulates partial allocation failure and verifies graceful fallback.

Suggested comments / phrasing for asynchronous feedback:
- "Thanks — quick pass. Can you add a short test exercising X (ref: edge-case list)? If you want I can pair on that for 20m."
- "Looks fine functionally, but I’m worried about potential perf regressions in the token loop — can you run perf profile (flamegraph) and attach results?"
- "If we keep this behavior, please add a note in the PR description about migration steps for existing cached checkpoints."

Refactor ideas spotted while scanning (note to self / follow-ups):
- Extract kernel-selection logic out of ModelRunner.run() into ModelRunner/kernels module. Right now kernel dispatch is entangled with request parsing. Cleaner separation would simplify testing and make perf isolation easier.
- Introduce a lightweight BatchContext object to carry telemetry + per-batch alloc hints rather than threading through maps in three layers.
- Replace ad-hoc retry wrapper in request handler with shared RetryPolicy util that supports exponential backoff + jitter. Several places replicate similar logic.

Post-merge actions to add to merge checklist (attach to PR before merge):
- Add rollout plan snippet in PR: canary percentage, duration, rollback criteria (error-rate spike, latency +50ms).
- Create a short smoke-job in infra/e2e that exercises this codepath with canary model/version. Link to job id.
- Add telemetry dashboards tile: latency p95/p99 for route, cache hit-rate; add alert (p95 > baseline + X ms).
- Tag release notes with concise line: what changed, who to contact if regression (include owner).
- If perf-sensitive, open a follow-up perf ticket with profiling artifacts and a labeled owner.

Mini template for post-merge comment to include automatically:
"Merged. Follow-ups: (1) e2e canary job run scheduled (infra/job/#####), (2) added smoke test ticket JIRA-XXXX, (3) perf profiling requested in ticket JIRA-YYYY. Revert plan: rollback to v<previous> if error-rate > 2% for 10m."

Known quick rejects (immediate block in async):
- Missing tests for a behavioral change.
- Secrets or raw credentials in code/logs.
- Schema or model format change without migration plan.
- Hard-coded region/zone or path that breaks private deployments.

Misc notes / personal reminders:
- When I’m low bandwidth: prioritize PRs with labels "blocking-release" or from owners SRE/Product.
- Use short code quotes in comments to point to exact lines. Examples: `// why this copy?` or `// potential hot path`
- If PR touches batching/cache, ask for perf numbers in PR description (before/after tokens/sec, p95 latency).

Scratchpad ideas to convert into small tasks later:
- Small RFC: "BatchContext and telemetry refactor" — outline API, migration path, and one small backwards-compatible change to validate (1 week).
- Add a dev-only OOM simulator harness to stress partial allocs in GPU memory (use CI gating via label).

Open questions to bring up in weekly sync:
- Should we require perf microbenchmarks on every PR that touches hot path? Cost vs benefit.
- How to better flag flaky tests in CI so reviewers can ignore transient failures?

——END——

(Quick link notes for myself: PR 4321 is the current change I'm reviewing — KV cache lifetime + batching tweaks; infra perf job id TBD)
